title_en: Regulations on the Administration of Gold and Silver of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to strengthen the management of gold and silver and to ensure the needs of the national economic construction for gold and silver.

Article 3 The State shall implement a policy of unified management, unified purchase, and unified allocation of gold and silver.
All receipts and expenditures of gold and silver by government organs, military units, social organizations, schools, state-owned enterprises, institutions, and urban and rural collective economic organizations within the territory of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter collectively referred to as domestic institutions) shall be incorporated into the State's gold and silver revenue and expenditure plan.

Article 4 The competent authority for the management of gold and silver under the State shall be the People's Bank of China.
The People's Bank of China shall be responsible for managing the State's gold and silver reserves; for the purchase and allocation of gold and silver; for formulating and managing the purchase and allocation prices of gold and silver in conjunction with the competent pricing authority of the State; for, in conjunction with the relevant competent authorities of the State, examining and approving units that operate (including processing and selling) gold and silver articles, gold- and silver-containing chemical products, and recover gold and silver from waste residues, waste liquids, and waste materials containing gold and silver (hereinafter collectively referred to as operating units), and for managing and inspecting the gold and silver market; and for supervising the implementation of these Regulations.

Article 5 All gold and silver held by domestic institutions must be sold to the People's Bank of China, except for raw materials, equipment, utensils, and souvenirs that have been permitted by the People's Bank of China for retention, and shall not be disposed of or retained by themselves.
Article 6 The State shall protect the holding of lawfully obtained gold and silver by individuals.

Article 7 Within the territory of the People's Republic of China, no unit or individual may use gold and silver for pricing, and private trafficking, lending, or mortgaging of gold and silver shall be prohibited.

Article 8 The purchase of gold and silver shall be handled uniformly by the People's Bank of China. No unit or individual may purchase gold or silver except with the permission or authorization of the People's Bank of China.

Article 9 All gold and silver extracted and smelted by factories, mines, enterprises, rural communes and brigades, military units, and individuals engaged in the production of gold and silver (including production from mineral deposits and as by-products of smelting) must be sold in full to the People's Bank of China, and shall not be sold, exchanged, or retained by themselves.
The production units listed in the preceding paragraph must strengthen the management of finished and semi-finished gold and silver products in the course of production in accordance with relevant provisions, and shall not sell or dispose of them privately.

Article 10 The State shall encourage operating units and units that use gold and silver to recover gold and silver from mineral species associated with gold and silver and from waste residues, waste liquids, and waste materials containing gold and silver.
The units listed in the preceding paragraph must sell the recovered gold and silver to the People's Bank of China, and shall not sell, exchange, or retain them by themselves, except that, with the permission of the People's Bank of China, units that use gold and silver may reuse the recovered gold and silver.

Article 11 All gold and silver imported from abroad by domestic institutions and gold and silver extracted as by-products from mineral products, except for gold and silver that have been permitted by the People's Bank of China for retention or that are used for processing imported materials for re-export in accordance with regulations, shall be sold to the People's Bank of China, and shall not be sold, exchanged, or retained by themselves.
Article 12 Any individual selling gold or silver must sell it to the People's Bank of China.

Article 13 All unearthed gold and silver without an owner shall be owned by the State, and no unit or individual may melt, destroy, or retain them.
Gold and silver unearthed and found without an owner by units or individuals shall, after being appraised by the local cultural administrative department, and except for those with historical cultural relic value which shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, must be delivered to the People's Bank of China for purchase, and the proceeds shall be turned over to the State treasury.

Article 14 All gold and silver confiscated according to law by State organs such as the public security, judicial, customs, administrative for industry and commerce, and tax authorities shall be sold to the People's Bank of China, and shall not be disposed of by themselves or substituted with other physical objects. The proceeds from the confiscated gold and silver shall be turned over to the State treasury in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 15 Any unit that needs gold and silver must submit a plan for the use of gold and silver to the People's Bank of China in accordance with the prescribed procedures, and the People's Bank of China shall approve and supply the gold and silver.
The People's Bank of China shall supply the gold and silver in accordance with the approved plan, and shall not arbitrarily reduce the supply or delay.

Article 16 Foreign-funded enterprises, Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures, and foreign businessmen within the territory of the People's Republic of China that order gold and silver articles or process other products containing gold and silver and require gold and silver to be supplied domestically must submit an application in accordance with the prescribed procedures, and the People's Bank of China shall examine and approve the supply.

Article 17 Units that use gold and silver must establish a usage system, strictly ensure special-purpose use, and return any surplus. Without the permission of the People's Bank of China, they shall not transfer gold and silver materials (including semi-finished products) or divert them to other uses.

Article 18 Within the scope provided for in these Regulations, the People's Bank of China shall have the authority to supervise and inspect units that use gold and silver. Units that use gold and silver shall truthfully provide the People's Bank of China with relevant information and materials concerning their use of gold and silver.

Article 19 Units that apply to operate (including processing and selling) gold and silver articles, gold- and silver-containing chemical products, and recover gold and silver from waste residues, waste liquids, and waste materials containing gold and silver must, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the examination and approval procedures, be examined and approved by the People's Bank of China and the relevant competent authorities, and after registering with the administrative authorities for industry and commerce and obtaining a business license, may commence business.

Article 20 Operating units must engage in business within the approved scope of gold and silver business, shall not change the business scope without authorization, and shall not short-change, misappropriate, or illicitly purchase gold and silver in the course of business.

Article 21 The minting and issuance of commemorative coins of gold and silver shall be handled by the People's Bank of China; no other unit may mint, counterfeit, or issue them.
The export operations of commemorative medals (plaques) of gold and silver shall be handled separately by the People's Bank of China and the Ministry of Foreign Economic Relations and Trade of the People's Republic of China.

Article 22 Consignment and commission shops shall not purchase or consign gold and silver articles or gold and silver materials. Jewelry stores may purchase jewelry with gold or silver inlay for export sale, but shall not purchase or sell gold and silver articles or gold and silver materials. Gold and silver articles shall be purchased by the People's Bank of China, which shall be responsible for supplying them for export trade.

Article 23 Individual silversmiths in frontier minority nationality areas and in areas with a relatively high concentration of overseas Chinese dependents along the coast may, with the approval of the People's Bank of China at or above the county level and the administrative authorities for industry and commerce, engage in the business of processing and repairing gold and silver articles for customers, but shall not purchase or sell gold and silver articles.

Article 24 The State permits individuals to mail gold and silver ornaments. The specific measures for management shall be formulated by the People's Bank of China in conjunction with the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications of the People's Republic of China.

Article 25 The quantity of gold and silver brought into the territory of the People's Republic of China shall not be subject to restrictions, but such gold and silver must be declared and registered with the Customs of the People's Republic of China at the place of entry.

Article 26 For gold and silver taken or brought out of the country, the Customs of the People's Republic of China shall, upon presentation of a certificate issued by the People's Bank of China or the quantity registered in the original declaration form at the time of entry, inspect and release the same; if no such certificate can be provided or the quantity exceeds that declared and registered at the time of entry, the gold and silver shall not be taken out of the country.

Article 27 For gold and silver ornaments (including inlaid ornaments, handicrafts, utensils, etc.) purchased by tourists within the territory of the People's Republic of China and taken out of the country, the Customs of the People's Republic of China shall, upon presentation of a special invoice issued by a domestic unit operating gold and silver articles, inspect and release the same. Without such supporting document, the gold and silver shall not be taken out of the country.

Article 28 For Chinese citizens, foreign nationals, and stateless persons within the territory of the People's Republic of China who leave the country for permanent residence, the limit for taking gold and silver per person shall be: one shi liang (31.25 grams) of gold ornaments, ten shi liang (312.50 grams) of silver ornaments, and twenty shi liang (625 grams) of silver utensils. Upon inspection by the Customs of the People's Republic of China and finding compliance with the prescribed limits, the Customs shall grant clearance.

Article 29 For foreign-funded enterprises and Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures within the territory of the People's Republic of China that import gold and silver from abroad as raw materials for products, the quantity shall not be subject to restrictions; for the export of products with a relatively high gold or silver content, approval from the People's Bank of China shall be obtained before customs clearance. Without such approval or in excess of the approved export quantity, the products shall not be taken out of the country.

Article 31 For the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the People's Bank of China, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce, and the Customs shall, according to the gravity of the circumstances and within their respective functions, powers, and jurisdictions, impose the following penalties:
(1) For violation of the provisions of Articles 8, 9, 10, and 11 of these Regulations, by purchasing, selling, exchanging, or retaining gold and silver without authorization, the People's Bank of China or the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall impose compulsory purchase or devalued purchase. If the circumstances are serious, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce may also impose a fine or solely impose confiscation.
For violation of the provisions of Articles 8, 9, 10, and 11 of these Regulations, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce may additionally impose the revocation of the business license.
(2) For violation of the provisions of Article 13 of these Regulations, by privately melting, destroying, or retaining unearthed gold and silver without an owner, the People's Bank of China shall recover the physical objects, or the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall impose a fine.
(3) For violation of the provisions of Article 17 of these Regulations, by changing the purpose of use without authorization or transferring gold and silver raw materials, the People's Bank of China shall give a warning or recover the gold and silver already allocated. If the circumstances are serious, a fine shall be imposed, and the supply may even be halted.
(4) For violation of the provisions of Articles 19, 20, 21, 22, and 23 of these Regulations, by operating without approval, or changing the business scope without authorization, or illicitly purchasing, misappropriating, or short-changing gold and silver, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall impose a fine or confiscation. If the circumstances are serious, they may also impose the revocation of the business license or order a suspension of business.
(5) For violation of the provisions of Article 7 of these Regulations, by using gold and silver for pricing, private trafficking, lending, or mortgaging, the People's Bank of China or the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall impose compulsory purchase or devalued purchase. If the circumstances are serious, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall impose a fine or confiscation.
(6) For violation of the provisions of Chapter V of these Regulations concerning the management of entry and exit of gold and silver, or smuggling gold and silver out of the country by any means, the Customs shall handle the matter in accordance with these Regulations and the national customs laws.
(7) For violation of the provisions of Article 14 of these Regulations, the People's Bank of China shall purchase the gold and silver. The administrative liability of the persons directly responsible shall be investigated by the relevant units.
Article 32 Where an act in violation of these Regulations constitutes a crime, the judicial authorities shall investigate the criminal liability according to law.
Article 33 The detailed rules for the implementation of these Regulations shall be formulated by the People's Bank of China in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 34 Where certain flexible provisions are needed for the management of gold and silver in frontier minority nationality areas, the relevant provincial or autonomous region people's governments shall, in conjunction with the People's Bank of China and in accordance with these Regulations, formulate such provisions.

Article 35 These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. The previous measures for the management of gold and silver formulated by the relevant departments shall be abolished simultaneously.
